Draw T iid samples, deterministic alpha_t>0, ell_t(x)=alpha_t f(x,xi_t). Any causal OCO algorithm, whose internal randomness is independent of samples, gives E[F(sum alpha_t x_t/sum alpha_t)]<=F(u)+E[Regret_T(u)]/sum alpha_t for every u in V.

Example3.2 context: finite N>=1 training pairs z_i in R^d, y_i in {-1,1}, R=max_i||z_i||_2, uniform iid training-point sampling, F(x)=N^(-1)sum max(1-y_i<z_i,x>,0), V=R^d, x_1=0. Example3.3: same setting, weighted losses ell_t(x)=max(1-y_t<z_t,x>,0)/(R sqrt(t)), constant OSD eta=1. Thus update is SGD with effective unweighted step1/(R sqrt(t)). For every minimizer x_star, E[F((sum x_t/sqrt(t))/(sum1/sqrt(t)))]-F(x_star) <= (||x_star||^2+sum1/t)/(2 sum1/(R sqrt(t))) <= R(||x_star||^2+1+ln T)/(4 sqrt(T+1)-4).

independent_directional_review.exact_arithmetic_proof: Let d=1, V=[-1,1], L=1, u=1, T=16 and ell_t(x)=g_t*x, with g_1=g_2=1, g_3=...=g_8=0, g_9=...=g_16=-1. The printed eta_t=sqrt(2)/(2*sqrt(t)) equals1/sqrt(2t). Algorithm2.2 plays x_t before updating x_(t+1)=clamp(x_t-eta_t*g_t). Thus x_1=0 and x_2=-1/sqrt2. Since1/sqrt2>1/2, x_2-eta_2<-1 and x_3=-1. Six zero gradients preserve x_3=...=x_9=-1. Each late eta_s with9<=s<=16 is strictly below1/4. Every partial sum of these eight increments is below2, so no late step clips at+1; increments are positive so no lower clipping. Therefore x_t=-1+sum_(s=9)^(t-1)1/sqrt(2s),9<=t<=17. The first two regret terms sum to-2-1/sqrt2; the zero-gradient terms vanish. Summing the eight late terms1-x_t yields16-sum_(s=9)^15(16-s)/sqrt(2s). Hence R_16=14-1/sqrt2-sum_(s=9)^15(16-s)/sqrt(2s). Because1/sqrt2<1, each1/sqrt(2s)<1/4 and sum_(s=9)^15(16-s)=28, R_16>14-1-28/4=6. Finally6>sqrt32 since36>32. This is an exact strict counterexample to R_T^direction(u)<=L*sqrt(2T) for this printed direction algorithm.
